question:
(a) Explain the meaning of work function of a metal and describe why an electron inside a metal cannot escape from the surface unless sufficient energy is supplied.
(b) A metal has work function $2.5\,\text{eV}$. Calculate the minimum energy in joule required to emit one electron from its surface. Take $1\,\text{eV} = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\,\text{J}$.

options.A:
(a) Work function is the maximum kinetic energy of electrons inside a metal; electrons escape when $E<\phi_0$.
(b) $2.5\,\text{eV}=2.5\times10^{-19}\,\text{J}$.
options.B:
(a) Electrons can always escape because they are free inside the metal.
(b) $2.5\,\text{eV}=1.56\times10^{19}\,\text{J}$.
options.C:
(a) Work function $\phi_0$ is the minimum energy needed for an electron to escape the metal surface. Electrons are bound by the surface potential due to positive ions and escape only if $E\geq\phi_0$.
(b) $\phi_0=2.5\times1.6\times10^{-19}=4.0\times10^{-19}\,\text{J}$.
options.D:
(a) Work function is the energy released when an electron enters a metal.
(b) $\phi_0=4.0\times10^{-20}\,\text{J}$.
